thread.title: Why Facebook’s stock plunge may gather steam

author: Anora M. Gaudiano
title: Why Facebook’s stock plunge may gather steam
text:
It has been an ugly day for Facebook, but things may get worse before they get better for the Menlo Park, Calif.–based social-media giant.
That is according to the data analysts at Bespoke Investment Group, who say that a double-digit percentage loss for a stock following quarterly results tends to gather steam toward the end of the regular trading session.
On Thursday, Facebook Inc. shares FB, -19.54% of the social network tumbled by as much as 20% after disappointing earnings, putting Thursday on track to erase more than $100 billion from the company’s market value. If it closes at this level, it would be the largest one-day decline since the company went public May 18, 2012, according to WSJ Market Data Group.
Bespoke’s analysis indicates that, on average, when a stock opens 15% or more lower after a company’s earnings report, as Facebook did Thursday, it tends to turn even weaker by the close of the trading day.
“Since 2001, 2,449 stocks have gapped down 15% or more on earnings. On average they have continued lower by 27 basis points from the open to the close of trading after the initial gap down,” the Bespoke report indicated.
That said, Bespoke acknowledges the temptation to buy the so-called dip. So far this year, buying stocks that dropped by double-digit percentages at the open and selling at the close would have been a good short-term trade, according to Bespoke. “We’ve seen 80 stocks gap down 15% or more on earnings so far in 2018, and they have averaged a gain of 91 bps from the open to the close following the initial gap down,” Bespoke said in a tweet.

The so-called FAANG stocks — Facebook, Apple Inc. AAPL, -0.06% , Amazon.com Inc. AMZN, -2.59% , Netflix Inc. NFLX, +0.27% and Google parent Alphabet Inc. GOOG, +0.28% GOOGL, +0.58% — historically have seen similar recoveries from the opening bell until close when they gapped down following earnings.
“When FAANG stocks specifically have gapped down 10% or more on earnings, they’ve averaged a gain of 1.34% from the open to the close,” Bespoke said in a tweet with the following chart, noting that its sample size was 28 instances beginning in 2001:
The last time Facebook’s stock fell 20%, which took a few weeks to accomplish, it didn’t take long for shares to recover as investors largely ignored the backlash to the company’s central role in the Cambridge Analytica data scandal .
The last time $FB dropped 20% it took 32 trading days to recover. pic.twitter.com/whVMGXPxbL
— Brian Lund (@bclund) July 25, 2018 How will Facebook perform this time around? Its long-term prospects remain unclear. Most sell-side analysts, however, are still reluctant to downgrade the stock in the wake of its current slide . But any further decline may change that.
